7. What are directions of the conventional current flow and electron flow?
8. What are conductor, insulator and semiconductor materials?
9. State Ohm’s law.
10. Show that, $V=IR$ using Ohm’s Law.
11. Plot a graph of $I$ versus $V$ on a graph paper for an Ohmic substance.
12. Define specific resistance.
13. Show that, the value of the equivalent resistance of resistors connected in series is equal to the sum of the different resistances included in the combination.
14. What are the causes of using electrical energy that can be dangerous?
15. A current of $2.5\text{ A}$ is flowing through the filament of the headlight of a motor car. If the potential difference between the two ends of the filament is $12\text{ V}$, what is the resistance?
16. The electromotive force of a dry cell is $1.5\text{ V}$. What is the energy spent by the cell in driving $0.5\text{ C}$ of charge round the circuit?
17. What are fixed and variable resistors?
18. What do you understand by electromotive force and potential difference?

1. Make a $2\text{ }\Omega$ resistor using infinite number of $1\text{ }\Omega$ resistor.
2. Using nichrome sheet of $1\text{ mm}$ thickness, your friend has made a resistor of $10\text{ cm} \times 10\text{ cm}$ square (Figure 11.18). You have made a resistor of $1\text{m} \times 1\text{m}$ square. What is the value of the resistance made by your friend? What is the value of your resistance?
